description_full: Sampo Oyj, together with its subsidiaries, provides non-life insurance products and services in Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia, Spain, Gibraltar, Germany, the Netherlands, France, and the United Kingdom. The company operates through Private Nordic, Private UK, Nordic Commercial, and Nordic Industrial segments. It offers property, casualty, liability, accident, sickness, household, homeowner, motor, travel, marine, aviation, transport, forest, livestock, health, workers compensation, car, van, and bike insurance, as well as reinsurance products under the If, Topdanmark, and Hastings brand names. Sampo Oyj was founded in 1909 and is based in Helsinki, Finland.

financial_summary: SAMPO PLC is a large-cap financial services business with a $26.6B market cap on $11.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +13% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

The business throws off $1.8B in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.88× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 6.6× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss.
Shareholder yield of 5.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 5.1% of the shares.
